item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Mexico’s biosecurity framework is described as grounded in national law, the Cartagena Protocol, the precautionary principle, and protection of health, biodiversity, food, and vulnerable groups. The diagnosis identifies unresolved needs for scientific risk assessment, risk classification, public technical information, interinstitutional coordination, and monitoring.","notes":["The excerpt supports the legal, precautionary, rights, protection, and unresolved-needs claims.","It does not support the claimed 2019–2024 measures, including glyphosate or genetically modified maize actions, an Indigenous consultation protocol, maize traceability work, or biodiversity targets."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The proposed biosecurity policy would establish independent multidisciplinary expert committees, systematic expert and international reviews, standardized risk protocols, differentiated regional and species-specific assessments, long-term post-release monitoring, integrated information and traceability systems, public reporting, consultation, and adaptive management.","notes":["The excerpt supports these as proposed lines of action.","It does not explicitly state that existing policy requires more technical, comprehensive, verifiable, and proportionate implementation; that rationale was removed."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt gives 2024 baselines of 30% and 40%, 2030 targets of 90% for both indicators, and states that no 2025 progress is reported because measurement is biennial."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports 2024 baselines of 40%, 31%, 35%, and 40%, with 2030 targets of 95%, 90%, 90%, and 95%, respectively."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the stated research-linkage diagnosis, 0.06% private-sector affiliation share, 1% allocation to the listed social-priority themes, technological dependence, and the 2023 high-technology-goods export/import figures and 1.15 coverage ratio.","The summary appropriately avoids assigning these aggregate outcomes to López Obrador."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL defines extreme poverty as income below the extreme-income poverty line plus at least three social deprivations. Between 2018 and 2022, multidimensional poverty fell from 41.9% to 36.3%, meaning approximately 5 million fewer people, while extreme poverty increased slightly from 7.0% to 7.1%. The report presents eradication as a government priority and identifies targeted interventions for highly deprived groups.","notes":["The excerpt says approximately 5 million people, not 5.1 million.","The remaining claims are supported."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports all listed 2022 deprivation percentages, the rise in health-service deprivation from 25.6% to 81.7% in the context of institutional reconfiguration, and the reported use of private facilities and pharmacy clinics among those seeking care."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports 45.1% of 9.1 million people, or 4.1 million, reporting no monetary social program, and the comparative health and food-access deprivation statement."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The proposed post-2024 poverty strategy combines pensions, disability support, child and education benefits, higher real minimum wages, and universal primary-care ambitions. For older adults in extreme poverty, 82.1% lacked health-service access, and 79.6% of poor older-adult program beneficiaries still had that deprivation in 2022.","notes":["The excerpt supports the listed proposed interventions and both health-service figures.","It does not explicitly state that a cash transfer alone would not secure social rights; that claim was removed."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0053-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the 2022 population, rural and demographic disparities, social-security and health deprivation, 784,000 children aged 3–17 out of school, and the recommendation to combine transfers with expanded social-rights coverage and services."]}]}
